story.title: XCancel service is suspended until further notice

draft:
When a payment‑cancellation service vanishes overnight, the impact hits far beyond a single API call.  

XCancel’s suspension forces every integration that relied on its webhook to confront an unexpected gap. I’ve seen similar shocks before—teams scramble to patch, roll back, or replace a critical component under pressure. The real lesson is that we need to treat third‑party services as “soft dependencies” and have a fallback ready before they become mission‑critical.

- Build a thin abstraction layer around external APIs so you can swap providers with minimal code churn.  
- Keep a local audit log of cancellation requests; it becomes a lifesaver when the upstream service goes dark.  
- Consider open‑source or self‑hosted alternatives for high‑risk flows; they add operational overhead but reduce vendor lock‑in.

I’m curious: what strategies have you put in place to keep your payment pipelines resilient when a partner service disappears?
